questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Indian Association in Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surendra Nath Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surendra Nath Banerjee:**

 
 
• Surendra Nath Banerjee, along with Anand Mohan Bose, founded the Indian Association in 1876.
 
• It was one of the earliest nationalist organizations in India, established to promote the political, intellectual, and material advancement of the Indian people.
 
• The Indian Association played a crucial role in mobilizing public opinion against discriminatory policies of the British government.
 
• It was a precursor to the Indian National Congress, and many of its members were instrumental in the Congress's formation.
 
• The association advocated for civil service reforms, the removal of racial discrimination, and the empowerment of Indians in governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chittaranjan Das:**

 
 
• Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as Deshbandhu, was a prominent Indian freedom fighter, political leader, and lawyer during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was a leading figure in Bengal during the Non-Cooperation Movement and later founded the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru.
 
• Das was known for his oratory skills and his dedication to the cause of Swaraj (self-rule).
 
• He served as the President of the Indian National Congress in 1922.
 
• His work focused on legal battles for political prisoners and advocating for greater autonomy for India, but he was not involved in the foundation of the Indian Association.
 
 
 
• **P Ananda Charlu:**
 
 
• P. Ananda Charlu was an early leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He served as the President of the Indian National Congress in 1891.
 
• He was a significant contributor to the early development of the Congress and its efforts to represent Indian interests.
 
• He was involved in legislative work, and contributed to the discussions of various bills.
 
• He was a well known lawyer.
 
• He was not involved in the founding of the Indian Association.
 
 
 
• **Rash Behari Bose:**
 
 
• Rash Behari Bose was a revolutionary leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was instrumental in organizing the Ghadar Conspiracy and later played a significant role in the formation of the Indian National Army (INA).
 
• He fled to Japan during World War II, where he continued to work for Indian independence.
 
• He handed over the INA to Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• His activities were more focused on revolutionary actions and armed struggle, rather than the earlier constitutional methods of the Indian Association.

questions.question: According to Newland's Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newlands' Law of Octaves:**

 
 
• John Newlands, an English chemist, proposed the Law of Octaves in 1865.
 
• He arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
 
• He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, much like the octaves in music.
 
• This law was an early attempt to find patterns in the properties of elements.
 
• The law was based on the atomic weights of the elements known at that time.
 
• The law was only applicable to elements up to calcium.
 
• Beyond calcium, the law failed because heavier elements did not follow the pattern.
 
• The periodic table was not fully developed at the time of Newlands.
 
• The later discovery of noble gases, also disrupted the octaves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P):**

 
 
• Nitrogen and Phosphorus belong to Group 15 (also known as the Nitrogen group or pnictogens) of the periodic table.
 
• They have similar chemical properties due to their similar electron configurations.
 
• Both have five valence electrons, which are the electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• This similarity in valence electrons leads to similar bonding behavior.
 
• Both can form covalent bonds.
 
• Both can form compounds with similar formulas.
 
• Both can have multiple oxidation states.
 
• Both are non-metals.
 
• Nitrogen and phosphorus are essential elements for life.
 
• They both can form acids.
 
• They both can form oxides.

questions.question: ________ is mainly celebrated by Maharashtrians as New Year's Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa:**

 
 
• Gudi Padwa is the Marathi New Year, celebrated primarily in Maharashtra and by Konkani Hindus.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra month, according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar, typically in March or April.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the new year and the arrival of spring.
 
• A "Gudi" (a decorated bamboo stick) is raised outside homes, symbolizing victory and prosperity.
 
• It is a time for festive meals, colorful decorations, and celebrating new beginnings.
 
• It is considered an extremely auspicious time, for new ventures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ugadi:**

 
 
• Ugadi is the New Year's Day for the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• It also falls on the first day of the Chaitra month.
 
• Like Gudi Padwa, it signifies the start of a new lunar year.
 
• It is celebrated with colorful decorations, special dishes, and religious observances.
 
• The creation of a special pachadi, which is a dish that contains all six tastes, is a very important part of the celebration.
 
 
 
• **Pongal:**
 
 
• Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It typically occurs in mid-January.
 
• It is a four-day festival dedicated to thanking the Sun God for a bountiful harvest.
 
• The festival involves preparing a dish called "Pongal" (sweet rice), decorating homes, and honoring cattle.
 
• The festival marks the end of winter, and the beginning of the suns northward journey.
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in the Indian state of Assam.
 
• Rongali Bihu, also called Bohag Bihu, is the Assamese New Year, celebrated in mid-April.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year and the spring season.
 
• The festival involves traditional dances, music, and feasting.
 
• It is a very colorful festival that brings the entire community together.

questions.question: Who among the following was sent by Akbar to lead the Mughal army in the Battle of Haldighati which was fought in 1576?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Man Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Man Singh:**

 
 
• Raja Man Singh I of Amber (Jaipur) was the commander-in-chief of the Mughal army during the Battle of Haldighati in 1576.
 
• He was a trusted general of Akbar and played a crucial role in expanding the Mughal Empire.
 
• He was instrumental in leading the Mughal forces against Maharana Pratap.
 
• His strategic military skills were highly valued by Akbar.
 
• He was a kachwaha Rajput and held a high mansab in the Mughal court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Todarmal:**

 
 
• Raja Todarmal was primarily known for his expertise in revenue and finance within Akbar's court.
 
• He implemented the "Zabti" system, a standardized system of revenue collection, which was a significant administrative reform.
 
• While he held a prominent position in Akbar's administration and was involved in military campaigns, his primary role was not leading the army in the Battle of Haldighati.
 
• He was one of the Navratnas in Akbars court.
 
• His work helped to stabalize the Mughal empires economy.
 
 
 
• **Raja Maharana Pratap:**
 
 
• Maharana Pratap was the ruler of Mewar and the primary adversary of the Mughal Empire in the Battle of Haldighati.
 
• He led the Rajput forces against the Mughal army, demonstrating fierce resistance.
 
• His bravery and dedication to defending his territory made him a symbol of Rajput valor.
 
• He refused to accept Akbars suzerainty.
 
• The battle of Haldighati was fought between his forces and the Mughal forces.
 
 
 
• **Raja Medini Rai:**
 
 
• Raja Medini Rai was a ruler of Chanderi and was involved in conflicts with the Mughal Empire before Akbar's reign, specifically with Babur.
 
• He was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Chanderi in 1528.
 
• He had no involvement in the Battle of Haldighati, which took place during Akbar's reign.
 
• He was a Rajput king.
 
• His battle with Babur occured long before the battle of Haldighati.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right guarantees protection of interests of the minorities in the matter of their language, script or culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cultural and Educational Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Cultural and Educational Rights:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, specifically Articles 29 and 30 of the Indian Constitution, guarantees the protection of the interests of minorities.
 
• Article 29 ensures that any section of citizens residing in India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script, or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Article 30 grants all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• This right is designed to safeguard the diverse cultural fabric of India and prevent any form of cultural assimilation. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• These rights enable minorities to preserve their unique identities and promote their educational and cultural development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Right to Equality:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution, ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and abolishes untouchability.
 
• While essential for a just society, it does not specifically address the protection of minority languages, scripts, or cultures.
 
• This right focuses on equal treatment under the law, not specific cultural preservation.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Right to Freedom:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution, guarantees various freedoms, including freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• It also protects against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• While these freedoms are vital for individual liberty, they do not directly provide for the protection of minority cultural and educational interests.
 
• This right focuses on individual liberties regarding actions and expression.
 
• While freedom of expression can be used to promote minority cultures, the right to freedom does not directly protect the culture itself.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Right against Exploitation:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution, prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and employment of children below the age of 14 in hazardous occupations.
 
• It aims to protect vulnerable sections of society from exploitation and abuse.
 
• While crucial for social justice, it does not pertain to the protection of minority languages, scripts, or cultures.
 
• This right is focused on preventing specific forms of human abuse and forced labour.
 
• This right is not related to cultural preservation.

questions.question: Select the odd one from the following saltwater lakes on the basis of their formation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sambhar lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sambhar Lake:**

 
 
• Sambhar Lake is a saltwater lake located in Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is India's largest inland salt lake.
 
• It is formed by inland drainage from several rivers.
 
• It is formed by the depression in the land, and the high evaporation rate of the arid region.
 
• It is a significant site for salt production and a habitat for migratory birds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kolleru Lake:**

 
 
• Kolleru Lake is a freshwater lake located in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in India.
 
• It is formed due to the flooding of the Krishna and Godavari river deltas.
 
• It acts as a natural flood-balancing reservoir between these two major rivers.
 
• It is a significant habitat for migratory birds.
 
 
 
• **Pulicat Lake:**
 
 
• Pulicat Lake is a saltwater lagoon located on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is the second-largest brackish water lagoon in India, after Chilika Lake.
 
• It is separated from the Bay of Bengal by the barrier island of Sriharikota.
 
• It is formed by the action of longshore currents and the deposition of sediments, creating a barrier lagoon.
 
• It is an important habitat for various aquatic birds, including flamingos.
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake:**
 
 
• Chilika Lake is a brackish water lagoon located in Odisha, India.
 
• It is the largest brackish water lagoon in India and one of the largest coastal lagoons in the world.
 
• It is separated from the Bay of Bengal by a narrow strip of land.
 
• It is formed by the deposition of sediments by rivers and the action of marine currents, creating a lagoon.
 
• It is a rich biodiversity hotspot and a Ramsar wetland of international importance.

questions.question: If the tax rate increases with the taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**progressive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Progressive:**

 
 
• A progressive tax system is one in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases.
 
• This means that higher-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes compared to lower-income earners.
 
• The intent of a progressive tax system is to distribute the tax burden more equitably, with those who have a greater ability to pay contributing a larger share.
 
• Income tax systems in many countries, including India and the United States, often use a progressive structure.
 
• Progressive taxation is often seen as a tool for reducing income inequality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regressive:**

 
 
• A regressive tax system is one in which the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases.
 
• This means that lower-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes compared to higher-income earners.
 
• Sales taxes and certain excise taxes can be considered regressive, as they take a larger proportion of income from those with lower incomes.
 
• Regressive taxes tend to exacerbate income inequality.
 
• These taxes place a higher burden on those who can least afford it.
 
 
 
• **Proportional:**
 
 
• A proportional tax system, also known as a flat tax, is one in which the tax rate remains constant regardless of the taxable amount.
 
• This means that everyone pays the same percentage of their income in taxes, regardless of their income level.
 
• While simple to administer, proportional taxes do not address income inequality.
 
• Everyone pays the same percentage of their income.
 
• This system is seen as being fair in that everyone is taxed at the same rate.
 
 
 
• **Digressive:**
 
 
• A digressive tax system is a tax system where the tax rate increases up to a certain point and then remains constant or decreases.
 
• It shares aspects of both progressive and proportional tax systems.
 
• It is less common than the other types of tax systems.
 
• The tax burden increases with income up to a specific income amount.
 
• After that amount the tax rate does not increase, or may decrease.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair (State and Iron-ore producing region) from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh - Ratnagiri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ratnagiri is located in the state of **Maharashtra**, not Madhya Pradesh, and is primarily known for bauxite deposits rather than iron ore.
 
• The major iron-ore producing regions in Madhya Pradesh include deposits in regions like **Jabalpur, Katni, and Sidhi**.
 
• Odisha is home to famous iron-ore regions such as **Badampahar, Keonjhar, and Sundergarh**.
 
• Kudremukh in Karnataka is one of the largest iron-ore mines in India and is renowned for its high-grade magnetite deposits.
 
• Chhattisgarh's Bailadila region is among the richest iron-ore reserves in India, particularly known for its **steel-grade hematite** deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Ore Deposits in India:**

 
 
• India ranks fourth globally in terms of iron ore production, following Australia, Brazil, and China.
 
• Major iron ore belts in India include Odisha-Jharkhand Belt, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur Belt, Bellary-Chitradurga Belt, and the Goa Belt.
 
• Odisha is the largest iron-ore producing state in India, contributing over 50% of the total output.
 
 
 
• **Types of Iron Ore:**
 
 
• **Hematite:** Contains up to 70% iron and is the most commonly mined ore in India.
 
• **Magnetite:** Contains up to 72% iron and is known for its magnetic properties.
 
• **Limonite and Siderite:** Lower grades of iron ore with less iron content.
 
 
 
• **Major Applications of Iron Ore:**
 
 
• Primarily used in the production of steel, which is a critical material for construction, automotive, and manufacturing industries.
 
• Iron ore is also used to make cast iron, wrought iron, and alloys like ferrochrome and ferromanganese.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Mining Iron Ore:**
 
 
• Mining activities can lead to deforestation, habitat destruction, and soil erosion.
 
• Proper implementation of sustainable practices and rehabilitation measures is necessary to minimize adverse effects.

questions.question: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was constructed in around 1197 AD by the sultan of which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamluk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mamluk:**
 
• The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was commissioned by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Mamluk dynasty (also known as the Slave dynasty).
 
• Construction began around 1193 AD and was completed in approximately 1197 AD.
 
• The mosque was built using the remains of demolished Hindu and Jain temples, reflecting the early Islamic conquests in India.
 
• It is considered one of the earliest existing mosques in India.
 
• The Mamluk dynasty was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lodhi:**
 
• The Lodhi dynasty was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526 AD.
 
• They were known for their architectural contributions, primarily tombs and gardens.

questions.question: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **plasmodesmata:**
 
• Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells.
 
• They facilitate the transport of materials, including water, nutrients, and signaling molecules, between adjacent cells.
 
• They are crucial for cell-to-cell communication and coordination within plant tissues.
 
• They allow for the symplastic transport of substances, meaning movement within the continuous cytoplasm of interconnected cells.
 
• They play vital roles in processes like nutrient distribution, signal transduction, and defense responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ribosomes:**
 
• Ribosomes are cellular organelles responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
 
• They consist of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
 
• They translate genetic information from messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains.
 
• They are essential for all living cells to produce the proteins necessary for cellular functions.
 
• **lysosomes:**
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells and some plant cells.
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• They play a crucial role in intracellular digestion and recycling.
 
• They are involved in processes like autophagy (self-digestion) and apoptosis (programmed cell death).
 
• They help to defend the cell against invading bacteria and viruses.
 
• **desmosomes:**
 
• Desmosomes are cell junctions that provide strong adhesion between animal cells.
 
• They are particularly abundant in tissues that experience mechanical stress, such as skin and muscle.
 
• They consist of proteins that link the cytoskeletons of adjacent cells.
 
• They contribute to the structural integrity and stability of tissues.
 
• They are not found in plant cells, as plant cell walls fulfill a structural role.

questions.question: Which executive system is present in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary System:**
 
• India follows a parliamentary system of government, which is derived from the Westminster model.
 
• In this system, the executive branch (the government) is responsible to the legislature (Parliament).
 
• The head of government is the Prime Minister, who is chosen from the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament).
 
• The President is the head of state, but their role is largely ceremonial.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility is a key feature, meaning the cabinet is jointly responsible to Parliament.
 
• The executive derives its power from the legislative body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collegiate System:**
 
• A collegiate system involves a group of individuals sharing executive authority.
 
• This system is not employed in India's national government.
 
• It is more commonly found in organizations or smaller governing bodies.
 
• It is not a system of government in the way that the parliamentary and presidential systems are.
 
• This type of system is not a common form of national government.
 
• **Both Parliamentary and Presidential System:**
 
• India does not have a hybrid system that combines both parliamentary and presidential features.
 
• The Indian Constitution clearly establishes a parliamentary form of government.
 
• There are no elements of a presidential system incorporated into the structure of the Indian government.
 
• The Indian constitution is very clear in its description of a parliamentary system.
 
• The separation of powers works in a very different way in a presidential system.
 
• **Presidential System:**
 
• In a presidential system, the President is both the head of state and the head of government.
 
• The President is elected independently of the legislature and has a fixed term of office.
 
• There is a clear separation of powers between the executive and legislative branches.
 
• The United States is a prominent example of a presidential system.
 
• India's constitution does not allow for a presidential system of government.
